key_insight: An agentic Gemini-based system can autonomously discover and Lean-verify compact acceleration rules for Busy Beaver Turing machines, extending AI from solving fixed math problems to uncovering new structure.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a practical pipeline for theorem-proving systems that combines pattern discovery, conjecture generation, and formal verification to study uncomputable or open-ended domains.
method: Scan Turing machine traces for repeated structure and candidate accelerations
Generate informal conjectures and compact mathematical rules from execution patterns
Formally verify discovered rules in Lean and classify confirmed cases
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the system autonomously discovered and formally verified novel Collatz-like accelerations for eleven machines in BB(6).
watch_item: The Cryptid classification is provisional and depends on community acceptance, so the results still require external validation of both the rules and the unresolved halting status.
paper_title: At the Limits of Computability: Steps Towards Autonomous AI Discovery on the Busy Beaver Frontier
